analysis.one_liner: ABB India makes electrification equipment and industrial automation gear (motors, drives, control systems) used in factories, utilities and infrastructure, and is majority owned by its Swiss parent ABB.
tags: Robotics business sold to parent in 2026
analysis.whats_happening: ABB India reported Q3 CY2026 results on 13 November 2026 (just three days before this report): revenue of ₹3,738 crore (+19% YoY) and net profit in the ₹440-443 crore range (+8-11% YoY, figures vary slightly by source). The standout number was order inflow of a record ₹4,733 crore, up 56% YoY, pushing the order backlog to roughly ₹13,000 crore (+36% YoY), with Electrification orders up a sharp 117% YoY on data-centre and energy-sector demand.
analysis.plain_terms: This is the Indian listing of global engineering major ABB, and it builds the unglamorous but essential stuff that keeps factories and power systems running - motors, switchgear, drives, and automation controls. Orders are growing very fast right now, especially from data centres, but the profit being made per rupee of sales has been getting thinner even as sales grow - that's the tension to watch. The company also sold off its robotics unit back to its Swiss parent in early 2026, so comparing this year's numbers to last year's needs a bit of care.
analysis.quarters: Revenue trend (consolidated, calendar-year quarters): Q4 CY25 ₹3,423cr/PAT ₹433cr → Q1 CY26 ₹3,184cr/PAT ₹362cr → Q2 CY26 ₹3,559cr/PAT ₹362cr → Q3 CY26 ₹3,738cr/PAT ~₹440-443cr. Revenue is up 19% YoY in the latest quarter but EBITDA margin (~15%) has compressed versus a year ago despite the growth - flagged by multiple outlets as 'order surge masking margin pressure.' Important non-comparability: ABB India divested its Robotics business to its Swiss parent for ₹2,367 crore (deal closed 1 March 2026), booking a one-time pre-tax gain of roughly ₹1,658 crore in Q1 CY26. That means the Q1 CY26 PAT figure (and any YoY comparison spanning it) includes a one-off item and isn't a clean read of operating profit; going forward the company reports only Electrification, Motion and Process Automation as segments.
analysis.performance_read: Over the last year the stock has sharply outperformed, up 45.87% versus the Nifty's -2.84% and peer Siemens India's 19.96% - but that one-year window captures a bounce from a weaker base; the 3-month return is actually negative (-7.77%, roughly in line with Siemens's -7.11%, both worse than the Nifty's +3.19%). The stock is 19.8% below its June 2024 peak of ₹8,796 - this is not the result of any split, bonus or demerger (the only logged corporate action is a 2007 5:1 split), so it represents a genuine price drawdown, not an accounting artefact. Separately, worth knowing for very long-term holders: ABB India demerged its Power Grids business to what is now Hitachi Energy India in 2019-2020, so anyone holding since before then also received separately-listed Hitachi Energy shares that don't show up in this stock's price chart - the return windows used here (3M/1Y/3Y/5Y) all start after that demerger, so they aren't distorted by it.
analysis.valuation_read: The stock trades around a P/E of ~93x and roughly 15-16x book value - this is expensive by almost any yardstick. It is expensive partly because the business is debt-free with high returns on capital (ROE ~22%, ROCE ~30%), and partly because the market is pricing in continued order-book momentum from electrification and data-centre spending. Whether that premium is justified depends on whether margins recover as the current order book converts to revenue - on today's numbers it is priced for a smoother growth story than the recent margin compression suggests.
analysis.growth_read: Growth right now looks more volume-led than margin-led: order inflow and revenue are both rising fast (orders +56% YoY, revenue +19% YoY), but the EBITDA margin has actually come down over the same period rather than expanded. That is a healthier combination than margin expansion on flat volumes, but it means profit growth is lagging revenue growth for now, and the market is betting on margins catching up as the bigger order book is executed.
analysis.health_read: ABB India is reported as almost debt-free, with strong ROE (~22%) and ROCE (~30%), which points to business-model strength rather than balance-sheet risk. The question mark is less about financial risk and more about execution/margin risk - whether the current order surge converts into profit growth at the same pace, or gets absorbed by input costs and competitive pricing. Cash conversion of profit was not independently verified in this pass and should be checked against the cash flow statement before relying on it.
analysis.ownership_read: The promoter - ABB Asea Brown Boveri Ltd, part of the Swiss ABB group - holds 75% of the company, unchanged, with zero shares pledged, which is a clean picture. Beyond that, sources disagreed on the exact FII/DII/public split (one source gave FII 2.4%/DII 9.8%, another gave FII 7.6%/DII 9.8%, a third gave DII as low as 1.1%) - these are internally inconsistent and should be checked directly on Screener or the BSE shareholding filing before being quoted precisely. Notable institutional holders mentioned across sources include LIC of India (~2-3%), BlackRock (~1%) and Norway's Government Pension Fund Global (~0.4%); there is no well-known individual Indian investor (the kind retail investors follow) on the register.
strengths: Record order inflow of ₹4,733 crore in Q3 CY2026, up 56% YoY, with the order book at ~₹13,000 crore (+36% YoY)
Electrification orders up 117% YoY on data-centre and energy-sector demand
Debt-free balance sheet with ROCE of ~30% and ROE of ~22%
Promoter holding stable at 75% with zero pledged shares
watchpoints: EBITDA margin has compressed even as revenue grew 19% YoY in the latest quarter - growth is currently outpacing profitability
Valuation is rich at roughly 93x earnings and ~15-16x book value, leaving little room for disappointment
The March 2026 robotics divestment and its one-time ~₹1,658 crore gain make quarter-on-quarter and year-on-year profit comparisons through CY2026 non-standard
Shareholding breakdown (FII/DII/public percentages) is inconsistent across available sources and needs direct verification before being cited precisely
analysis.one_thing: Whether the EBITDA margin recovers in Q4 CY2026 as the elevated order book starts converting to revenue - that is what will show whether this is durable, margin-accretive growth or just volume growth absorbing cost pressure.
analysis.data_notes: Cross-checked Q3 CY2026 revenue, order inflow and order-book figures across Business Standard, Screener.in, Upstox and GuruFocus - these were consistent. The exact PAT figure varied between ₹440-443 crore across outlets and is reported as a range rather than a single precise number. The robotics divestment (closed 1 March 2026, ₹2,367 crore, ~₹1,658 crore one-time pre-tax gain) was corroborated by multiple secondary sources citing BSE filings but no primary exchange filing was directly reviewed. FII/DII/public shareholding percentages conflicted materially across sources and were NOT independently verified - treat ownership percentages beyond the 75% promoter stake with caution. A cited debt figure (~₹52 crore) referenced a balance sheet date from December 2024 and may be stale; current debt level was not independently confirmed for this quarter.
